cost.description: Resources supporting the FAIR management of OCDM include its public specification and documentation, version control through the OpenCitations GitHub repository, and versioned releases deposited in Figshare.
Resources supporting the management and reuse of the Index ingestion software include the public OpenCitations GitHub repository, version control, source code, configuration files and tests
Resources supporting the FAIR management of oc_ocdm include its public GitHub repository, documentation, version control, automated tests, dependency management and published software packages.
Resources supporting FAIR management of the OpenCitations Index include the ingestion workflow, provenance and change-tracking information, public data dumps, REST APIs and the SPARQL endpoint.

Resources supporting FAIR management of OpenCitations Meta include its automated curation and RDF-conversion workflow, provenance and change tracking, public dataset distributions, APIs and the SPARQL endpoint.

Resources supporting the management and reuse of oc_meta include its public GitHub repository, version control, source code, tests, software releases and the documented automated curation and RDF-generation workflow.

data_quality_assurance: OCDM reuses established ontologies and follows a documented ontology development and evaluation process. Extensions use SAMOD with motivating scenarios, competency questions, and a glossary of terms. OCO has been evaluated against JATS/XML data, compared with other bibliographic data models, and tested against requirements from early adopters. New use cases are used to identify and address gaps in the model.
dataset.description: The OpenCitations Data Model is an RDF-based model for representing bibliographic entities, citations, identifiers, agents, publication venues, and provenance. It reuses the SPAR Ontologies, PROV-O, and other established vocabularies to provide a consistent semantic representation across OpenCitations datasets and external projects.
keyword: OpenCitations, OpenCitations Data Model, OCDM, bibliographic metadata, citation data, RDF, Semantic Web, SPAR Ontologies, provenance

metadata.description: The Figshare record includes structured metadata for the title, creators, description, keywords, license, DOI, publication date, and version. Figshare exposes these metadata in machine-readable formats through its API and metadata export services.

dataset.preservation_statement: The OCDM specification, ontology documentation, examples, development and evaluation materials, and previous published versions will be preserved. Earlier versions document changes to the model and support the interpretation of data created under older versions.
dataset.title: OpenCitations Data Model (OCDM)

data_quality_assurance: Development is managed with Git and supported by an automated test suite and GitHub workflows. Static type checking is performed with Pyright, and code changes can be reviewed through GitHub pull requests. Data produced by the ingestion workflow is also subject to validation and post-ingestion monitoring.
dataset.description: oc-index is a Python package for producing citation data for the OpenCitations Index. It resolves external identifiers in citation tables to OpenCitations Meta Identifiers (OMIDs), converts citation links into OMID-to-OMID relationships, and generates citation entities compliant with the OpenCitations Data Model. The software is open source and released under the ISC License.
keyword: OpenCitations, OpenCitations Index, citation ingestion, research software, Python, OMID, OCI, RDF, OpenCitations Data Model, Linked Open Data

metadata.description: The repository includes structured software metadata for the name, version, description, license, author contact, Python requirements, dependencies, and command-line entry points in pyproject.toml. GitHub records the development history, while Software Heritage records the archived software snapshot.

dataset.preservation_statement: Source code, version history, configuration files, documentation, tests, and released versions will be preserved. Earlier versions support the reproduction of historical ingestion workflows and OpenCitations Index releases.
dataset.title: oc-index (OpenCitations Index software)
dataset.type: Application software for citation data ingestion and transformation

data_quality_assurance: oc_ocdm uses Test Driven Development, automated tests, benchmarks, and GitHub workflows to check software changes. The library also validates entity operations against OCDM constraints. Change tracking and provenance record modifications to RDF entities, while versioned releases and the changelog document changes to the software.
dataset.description: oc_ocdm is an open-source Python library for creating and manipulating RDF data compliant with the OpenCitations Data Model. It provides object-oriented interfaces for bibliographic resources, agents, identifiers, provenance, and dataset metadata, with support for validation, change tracking, serialization, and synchronization with RDF stores. The software is released under the ISC License.
keyword: OpenCitations, oc_ocdm, OpenCitations Data Model, OCDM, Python, RDF, SPAR Ontologies, provenance, Semantic Web, object mapping

metadata.description: oc_ocdm includes structured metadata for its name, creators, version, license, Python requirements, repository, release information, and citation information. The source repository provides these through files including pyproject.toml, CITATION.cff, CHANGELOG.md, and README.md, while Zenodo and PyPI expose metadata for published releases.

dataset.preservation_statement: Source code, released packages, version history, tests, documentation, configuration files, and software metadata will be preserved. Earlier releases are retained because OpenCitations applications may depend on specific versions and because they support reproducibility.
dataset.title: oc_ocdm (software for handling OCDM-compliant data)
dataset.type: Python software library for RDF object mapping, data manipulation, and provenance management

data_quality_assurance: The ingestion workflow normalises external identifiers and uses OpenCitations Meta to map identifiers referring to the same bibliographic resource. These mappings allow duplicate citation links from different sources to be identified and removed. Provenance and change-tracking records support traceability, while validation is applied before publication.
dataset.description: The OpenCitations Index is an open collection of citation links integrated from multiple scholarly data sources. Citations are normalised as OMID-to-OMID relationships, deduplicated, and represented according to the OpenCitations Data Model. Each citation is identified by an Open Citation Identifier (OCI) and can include metadata, provenance, and change-tracking information.
keyword: OpenCitations, OpenCitations Index, citations, bibliographic metadata, RDF, Linked Open Data, provenance, OCI, OMID

metadata.description: Index citations include identifiers for the citing and cited resources, citation metadata where available, and provenance records describing their source and history. Figshare records provide descriptive metadata and persistent DOIs for the published distributions.

dataset.preservation_statement: Citation data, provenance, change-tracking information, published distributions, and previous dataset dumps will be preserved. Earlier dumps record the state of the Index at different points in time and support reproducibility.
dataset.title: OpenCitations Index

data_quality_assurance: Before RDF conversion, the Curator performs identifier-based deduplication, enrichment, normalization, and error correction. Entities are merged only when shared identifiers establish that they represent the same resource. Provenance and change-tracking records preserve the history of each entity. META-CSV data can be validated before ingestion, and automated monitoring queries can detect database-level errors after ingestion.
dataset.description: OpenCitations Meta is an open bibliographic metadata database for scholarly resources involved in citations indexed by OpenCitations. Records are automatically curated and deduplicated using persistent identifiers, and entities are assigned OpenCitations Meta Identifiers (OMIDs). Curated metadata are represented as OCDM-compliant RDF, with provenance and change-tracking records documenting the source and history of each entity.
keyword: OpenCitations, OpenCitations Meta, bibliographic metadata, OMID, RDF, Linked Open Data, provenance, change tracking, data curation

metadata.description: Published distributions include repository metadata for the title, creators, description, publication date, license, version, and persistent identifiers. Within OpenCitations Meta, bibliographic records contain structured metadata and identifiers, while provenance records document their source and modification history.

dataset.preservation_statement: Curated bibliographic metadata, OMID mappings, provenance records, change-tracking information, published distributions, and previous releases will be preserved. Earlier releases document the state of the database at different points in time and support reproducibility and historical analysis.
dataset.title: OpenCitations Meta

data_quality_assurance: oc_meta is maintained with Git and an automated test suite integrated with GitHub workflows. Development tools include pytest and coverage for testing, Pyright for static type checking, and Ruff for code analysis. Software changes are documented through versioned releases and the project changelog.
dataset.description: oc_meta is open-source Python software for managing bibliographic metadata in OpenCitations Meta. It processes structured CSV metadata, performs automated curation, and generates RDF compliant with the OpenCitations Data Model. The software also records provenance and change tracking for bibliographic entities and is released under the ISC License.
keyword: OpenCitations, OpenCitations Meta, oc_meta, bibliographic metadata, Python, RDF, OMID, provenance, data curation, Semantic Web

dataset.preservation_statement: Source code, released packages, version history, configuration files, documentation, tests, and software metadata will be preserved. Earlier releases are retained to support the reproducibility of previous OpenCitations Meta processing workflows.
dataset.title: oc_meta (OpenCitations Meta software)

dmp.description:
This Data Management Plan describes the management of the main data, data models, and software components of the OpenCitations infrastructure.
It covers the OpenCitations Data Model(OCDM), OpenCitations Index, OpenCitations Meta, and the software used to ingest, process, validate, and manage data compliant with the OpenCitations Data Model.
The purpose of the plan is to document how these research objects are created, processed, stored, documented, accessed, shared, preserved, and reused, including their formats, identifiers, provenance, licensing, and data quality procedures.
The DMP is intended to provide a structured and machine-actionable description of the data management practices adopted within OpenCitations.
dmp.title: OpenCitations Data Management Plan
